question: Should Gateway allow scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if so should that live in existing `allowedOrigins` syntax or a constrained pattern field?
rationale: This changes the browser-origin authorization boundary for Gateway WebSocket clients, and current related PRs prove demand but do not establish the permanent wildcard grammar or security posture.

options.title: Define constrained pattern contract
options.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, tests, docs, and audit behavior for extension/custom-scheme origin patterns instead of accepting arbitrary trailing-prefix wildcards.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Land or review exact opaque-origin fixes and close the changing-extension-ID wildcard request as outside the current security policy.

options.title: Allow `chrome-extension://*` in `allowedOrigins`
options.body: Take the minimal user-facing syntax, but require narrow scheme-only matching and negative security tests before merge.

recommendation.title: Define constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, tests, docs, and audit behavior for extension/custom-scheme origin patterns instead of accepting arbitrary trailing-prefix wildcards.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and repeatedly tightened the current Gateway browser-origin policy and merged the existing global wildcard support.
